items.title: Introduction
items.text:
Zettel Notes is a Markdown note-taking app for Android. Your notes stay as plain-text files in folders you control, so no app ever locks you in.

Download Privacy Policy

items.title: Why Zettel Notes?
items.text:
• Plain-text files. Every note is a separate Markdown, text or Org file that any other app can open.
  • Use your existing notes. Add any folder as a repository and your notes appear immediately.
  • Free, with no ads. No hidden permissions and no collection of user data.
  • Offline first. Everything works without an internet connection; sync is optional.

items.title: Getting started
items.text:
1. Install Zettel Notes. The app opens with an introductory note.
  2. Open the menu, select Repositories, and add the folder that holds your notes (or start fresh in the app's own folder).
  3. Read about notes, the editor and Markdown formatting.

items.title: Features
items.text:
Writing and linking

  • Markdown formatting with LaTeX, tables and task lists
  • Zettelkasten support: wiki links, backlinks, tags and authors
  • Note types: task, drawing, audio, bookmark and log notes
  • Templates and YAML frontmatter
  • Citation manager for BibTeX and CSL JSON

Organising and finding

  • Multiple repositories with subfolders; MD, TXT and Org files
  • Full-text search and saved searches
  • Sort by name, edit time, creation time, word count or how often a note is opened
  • Bookmark and pin notes, calendar view, gallery and recycle bin

Sync and security

  • Git, Dropbox, WebDAV and SFTP sync with a built-in keys manager
  • Note encryption with a password or PGP key
  • App lock with biometrics
  • Automatic backups

Customisation and integration

  • App themes, Markdown styles and fonts
  • Keyboard shortcuts
  • Share notes as PDF, HTML, launcher shortcuts, widgets or pinned notifications
  • Clip web pages or share text from any app into a note
  • Tasker integration and plugins

items.title: App Lock
items.text:
To lock the app, go to Settings > Security, select App Lock and choose Passcode. Enter a passcode and confirm. You will be asked for it whenever the app restarts or the lock timeout expires.

Info

To unlock with your fingerprint, enable Biometrics on the App Lock screen.

To change the timeout, adjust Lock Timeout (in minutes). The maximum is 30 minutes.

When a timeout is set, a lock button appears on the notes screen. Tap it to lock the app immediately.

Timeout button in menu

items.title: Backups
items.text:
Zettel Notes can back up your notes automatically at a set interval.

Info

Automatic backups include only notes in the App Folder. Notes in external folders are not backed up.

To enable automatic backups:

  1. Go to Menu > Settings > Backup and Restore
  2. Turn on Enabled under Automatic backups
  3. Select backup folder and backup interval
  4. Tap Backup Now to create a backup immediately

Tip

To create a local backup inside application data (not accessible via file explorer), click on first option Backup (excluding external notes). Share the backup file with your favourite application.

Auto Backup Settings

Available intervals:

  • 30 mins
  • 1 hour
  • 6 hours
  • 12 hours
  • Daily
  • Weekly

items.title: Backup options
items.text:
• What to include: choose which data goes into a backup. Font files can be included v3.0.7.
  • Password protection: encrypt automatic backups with a password in Settings > Backup and Restore v2.9.8. Without the password, the backup cannot be restored.
  • Retention: keep only a maximum number of backup files v2.8.4, or delete backups older than a chosen number of days.

items.title: Other data you can back up
items.text:
Besides the full app backup, these can be backed up and restored on their own:

  • Markdown buttons and editor toolbar buttons
  • Text snippets
  • Saved searches
  • Keyboard shortcuts
  • Fonts
  • Templates and themes (exported together)
  • Memo notes (export and import)

items.title: Restore a backup
items.text:
Tap Restore backup in Backup and Restore. Backups stored in app data are listed; select one to restore. To restore from external storage or your backup folder, tap Select from storage.

File Selection for Restoring backup

In the restore dialog, choose what to restore from the data contained in the backup, such as Databases, Settings and Templates. If the backup is password-protected, you are asked for the password.

Restore Dialog

Warning

Reset to default erases all app data. It cannot be undone.

items.title: BibTeX
items.text:
Zettel Notes includes a citation manager that reads BibTeX (.bib) and CSL JSON (.json) files.

  1. Go to Menu > Repositories
  2. Edit specific repository and click on BibTex File
  3. Select your citations bib or json file from internal storage.
  4. Save the repository.
  5. To browse this BibTex file, Select BibTex from left navigation drawer on main screen.

To export a citations file from Zotero, see this guide.

items.text:

  • Download via Play Store or F-Droid

items.title: Change the bibliography style (CSL)
items.text: On the BibTeX screen, open the top-right menu and select CSL Style manager. Tap Download to choose from over 2,500 citation styles.

items.title: Download
items.text:
Zettel Notes is available from the Play Store and from its own F-Droid repository.

  • Google Play Store
  • F-Droid repository

items.title: F-Droid repository
items.text:
The F-Droid repository carries Zettel Notes, its plugins and the developer's other apps, and delivers updates through your F-Droid client.

  1. Install an F-Droid client: Droid-ify (recommended) or the official client.

  2. Add this repository:

    https://thedoc.eu.org/fdroid/repo

  3. Check that the fingerprint matches:

    B1358F5B942E5676B2935B83F39E3BAA363F3FDA9E53DB62113551D14B09A173

If downloads are slow, use the mirror URL.

items.title: Beta testing
items.text:
1. Join the Google Group.
  2. Sign up at https://play.google.com/apps/testing/org.eu.thedoc.zettelnotes.

items.title: Frequently Asked Questions
items.text: Answers to the questions asked most often in GitHub issues and Discussions.

items.title: How can I open my existing notes?
items.text:
Add the folder that contains them as a repository: open the main menu, select Repositories and tap +. Zettel Notes reads every supported file in that folder and its subfolders, and edits are saved straight back to the same files.

To keep using another app (such as Obsidian) on the same notes, add the same folder, or sync both apps to the same Git, Dropbox, WebDAV or SFTP location.

items.title: Where are notes in the App Folder stored?
items.text:
In the app's private storage, which other apps and file managers cannot access:

/data/data/org.eu.thedoc.zettelnotes/notes

To reach these files from other apps, mount internal repositories so they appear in the Android Files (Documents) app, or use Git sync. The Storage Manager shows how much space they use.

items.title: Why can't I attach any file from my phone's storage?
items.text: Android's scoped storage stops apps from reading arbitrary files. Zettel Notes can only open files inside its own storage, inside a repository folder you added, or a file you pick through the system file picker. This protects your privacy and cannot be bypassed by the app.

items.title: Which characters can't I use in filenames?
items.text:
Zettel Notes follows the same filename rules as Dropbox, so that notes sync everywhere. These characters are not allowed and are replaced when you create or rename a note:

/ \ < > : " | ? * .

items.title: Why does the Notes List show the wrong creation date, or 00:00 as the time?
items.text:
Android does not record when a file was created, and sync changes the file's dates. Store the date in the filename or in the frontmatter instead. The date: value must use the format yyyyMMddHHmmss, e.g. date: 20261028143000. Other formats such as 2026-10-28 14:30 are not recognised.

See Note Creation Date for the step-by-step setup.

items.title: Why does the note preview show fewer lines than "Content Max Lines"?
items.text: To keep the notes list fast, only the first 50 words of each note are loaded for the preview. If those 50 words fit in fewer lines than your Content Max Lines setting, the preview is shorter, and the last word may be cut off.

items.title: Why does a widget or the Notes List show a different title than I expected?
items.text: The title comes from your repository's Prefer Title From setting: YAML title, first heading, filename or first line. To always show filenames, enable the filename option in Settings > Notes List.

items.title: Why does searching for key: value from YAML find extra notes?
items.text:
Search uses SQLite full-text search, which matches words rather than exact text. appbar: teal finds every note containing the word appbar followed later by the word teal, not only notes with that exact line.

To narrow it down, add more words from the line you want, or open the note from Attributes in the left drawer, which lists the values of each YAML property.

items.title: Why doesn't a search that starts with -word exclude anything?
items.text: An excluding term (-word) only works after at least one normal term. Search ideas -draft, not -draft on its own. See Search syntax.

items.title: I changed a note on my computer, but the app still shows the old version
items.text:
After a sync, Zettel Notes rescans downloaded files in the background, which can take a moment for large files or repositories.

  1. Wait a few seconds and pull down to refresh the notes list.
  2. Check the sync log: a line such as download /notes/Note.md means the file arrived.
  3. Open the file with your phone's file manager to confirm its content.
  4. If the file is up to date but the app is not, report it in an issue with your sync method and the sync log.

items.title: How do I sync safely with Obsidian or another app?
items.text:
• Let the first Git clone finish completely before editing anything. If the clone shows an error, delete the repository in Zettel Notes and add it again rather than continuing.
  • Sync before you start editing on a device, and again when you finish.
  • Avoid editing the same note on two devices before they have synced.
  • Choose how conflicts are handled in Conflict Resolution.
  • Keep automatic backups turned on.

items.title: How do I use Nextcloud?
items.text:
Use WebDAV sync with your Nextcloud WebDAV URL:

https://SERVER/remote.php/dav/files/USERNAME/SUBFOLDER/

Replace SERVER with your Nextcloud address, USERNAME with your Nextcloud username and SUBFOLDER with the folder to sync, e.g. https://thedoc.eu.org/nextcloud/remote.php/dav/files/dax/znotes/.

items.title: How do I get back a deleted or overwritten note?
items.text:
Try these in order:

  1. Recycle bin: deleted notes stay in each repository's recycle bin for 7 days by default.
  2. Note history: open the note in the editor and use the Revision button to restore an earlier version.
  3. Backups: restore from an automatic backup.
  4. Sync history: with Git sync, earlier versions are in the repository's commit history (Git settings > List Commits).

items.title: Can I edit two notes side by side?
items.text: Not reliably yet. Editing two notes at the same time in split screen or Samsung DeX has caused one note to overwrite the other (issue #451). Until this is fixed, edit one note at a time.

items.title: How does encryption work?
items.text: Zettel Notes offers four methods: end-to-end, password-based, OpenPGP and in-app PGP key. Your password is never stored, so if you lose it, encrypted notes cannot be recovered. See Note Encryption.

items.title: How do I get updates without the Play Store?
items.text: Add the Zettel Notes F-Droid repository to an F-Droid client.

items.title: F-Droid downloads are slow
items.text:
The F-Droid repository server can occasionally be slow. If so, use this mirror instead:

https://gitlab.com/royalhacker/fdroid-live/-/raw/master

items.title: How do I become a beta tester?
items.text:
1. Join the Google Group.
  2. Sign up at https://play.google.com/apps/testing/org.eu.thedoc.zettelnotes.

items.title: Where do I report a bug or request a feature?
items.text:
• Bugs: open an issue. Include your app version, Android version, device, the steps to reproduce, and screenshots or a screen recording.
  • Feature requests and questions: start a discussion. Vote on existing requests instead of opening duplicates.

items.title: Gallery and Media
items.text:
The Gallery shows all media files in a repository, including images, PDFs and other attachments.

To open it, open the left navigation drawer and tap Gallery. Use the filter chips at the top to show only certain types of file v2.9.1.

Gallery showing Media Files

Long-press a media file to:

  1. Rename it
  2. Copy its link to paste into a note
  3. Show the notes that use it
  4. Open it in the system file manager
  5. Create a launcher shortcut that opens it directly
  6. Delete it

Tip

To find media files no note links to, tap Toggle Unused Media in the top-right menu.

items.title: Images
items.text:
• Image viewer: images open in the built-in viewer, which shows all the images in the note.
  • Image editor: edit images from the Gallery v2.6.1.
  • Open with another app: open an image in another installed app v3.1.0. Images hosted online open in an in-app web view v3.1.1.
  • Paste from clipboard: paste images from the clipboard into the editor v2.6.5.
  • Animated GIFs play in view mode.

For image syntax, size and alignment, see Formatting.

items.title: Audio
items.text: Audio attachments, including recordings in audio notes, play in the built-in audio player v2.6.4.

items.title: PDFs and other files
items.text:
• ![](file.pdf) shows a preview of the PDF in view mode v2.8.8.
  • A link to any other file, e.g. [Report](report.docx), opens it in the matching Android app (documents, spreadsheets, presentations, audio, video and more).

items.title: Where attachments are saved
items.text: New attachments go to the folder set in the repository's default location for attachments. Their filenames follow the attachment suffix set in Settings > Editor and Viewer > Attachment Suffix (see Drawing Note).

items.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
items.text:
Zettel Notes supports hardware keyboards. Built-in actions can be triggered with key combinations, and every shortcut can be remapped.

To view or change shortcuts, go to Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts.

Keyboard Shortcuts

items.title: What you can do with shortcuts
items.text:
• Insert headings v1.0.70
  • Open text snippets v2.7.9
  • Run any of the built-in editor actions

Tip

On a touch screen without a hardware keyboard, the meta keys toolbar editor button shows keys such as Ctrl and the arrow keys, so you can still use shortcuts v2.9.1.

items.title: Back up your shortcuts
items.text: Custom shortcuts can be backed up and restored with the rest of your app data v2.7.9.

items.title: Navigation
items.text: Zettel Notes has two side drawers: the left drawer for moving between repositories and collections of notes, and the right drawer for working within the open note.

items.title: Left drawer
items.text:
Open it with the menu button or by swiping right on the notes list v2.9.2.

It contains:

  • Repositories: switch between repositories. You can also long-press the home button to change repository quickly.
  • Recent notes: the notes you opened most recently.
  • Saved searches, with the number of matching notes.
  • Attributes: tags, authors and any YAML property you add with Add Attribute. Tap a value to search for it.
  • Calendar, Gallery and BibTeX.
  • Installed plugins.
  • The sync button, for manual synchronization.

To choose which sections appear, go to Settings > Notes List.

items.title: Right drawer
items.text:
v2.9.5

The right drawer has four tabs:

Tab Shows Outline The headings of the open note; tap one to jump to it Navigation Navigation history; long-press an entry to pin or unpin it Backlinks Notes that link to the open note Tags Tags

The Memo can also be opened from the right drawer.

items.title: Folders
items.text:
Repositories can contain subfolders. A breadcrumb (folder navigation) bar at the top of the notes list shows the current folder path.

Folders can be renamed and deleted from the notes list. To open a folder from inside a note, use a folder link such as [sub-folder](/sub-folder/).

items.title: Notes List
items.text: The notes list is the main screen of Zettel Notes. It shows the notes and folders of the current repository.

items.title: Layouts
items.text:
Choose between three layouts v2.2.0:

  • Compact
  • Normal
  • Grid

In Settings > Notes List you can also:

  • show or hide note content, and set how many lines and what text size it uses (the preview is built from the first 50 words of the note, so it can be shorter than the line limit)
  • show the filename instead of, or with, the title
  • show an icon for each note type (Modify Info Shown > Icons)
  • turn the divider between notes on or off v3.0.2
  • adjust corner radius, padding and text size (Display)
  • customise the add note button

items.title: Sorting
items.text: Notes can be sorted alphabetically, by edit time, by creation time, by word count, by filename, or by how often they are opened. For reliable creation dates, see Note Creation Date.

items.title: Selecting several notes
items.text:
Long-press a note to start multi-selection, then tap other notes to add them v2.1.4. With several notes selected you can:

  • Copy or move them to another folder or repository
  • Share them
  • Delete them (they go to the recycle bin)

items.title: Bookmark and pin
items.text: Notes can be bookmarked or pinned from the notes list. You can also bookmark a note from its frontmatter with bookmark: true (see YAML Frontmatter).

items.title: Folders
items.text: Tap a folder to open it; the breadcrumb bar at the top shows the current path. Folders can be renamed or deleted. See Navigation.

items.title: Recycle Bin
items.text:
Each repository has its own recycle bin.

The recycle bin is enabled by default and automatically empties items older than 7 days. You can change this in Settings to any value up to 30 days. Set it to 0 to keep deleted files indefinitely.

Info

Restored files return to the folder they were deleted from.

items.title: Search
items.text: Zettel Notes indexes the contents of every note, so full-text search returns results almost instantly.

items.title: Search syntax
items.text:
Query Finds notes that contain tag tag1 both words tag OR tag1 either word tag -tag1 tag but not tag1 (an excluded term needs at least one normal term before it) tag* words starting with tag #tag the tag #tag
  • Matching is fuzzy, so close variations of a word are also found.
  • The characters #, @, _, - and / can be used in queries, so you can search for tags, authors and paths v2.8.9.
  • The search runs when you press Enter.
  • In the notes list, tag searches can be applied one after another to narrow the results (sequential tag search) v2.9.2.

Tip

Search can be limited to the current subfolder with the restrict-search-to-subfolder option in settings.

items.title: Sort and filter results
items.text: To sort or filter results, tap the Sort icon in the menu. Results can be sorted by Date, Title, Word Count, Last Modified, Times Accessed and Filename.

items.title: Search inside a note
items.text:
In view mode, use the search button to find text within the open note, and the previous and next buttons to move between matches.

To find and replace text while editing, see Search and replace.

items.title: Search by attribute
items.text: The Attributes section of the left drawer lists tags, authors and other frontmatter properties. To search by any YAML property, go to Left drawer > Add Attribute and choose the property v2.9.0. Its values then appear in the drawer and can be tapped to search.

items.title: Saved searches
items.text:
Frequently used queries can be saved. They appear under Saved Searches in the left navigation drawer, with the number of matching notes.

Left Navigation Drawer

To manage them, tap Edit in the Saved Searches section and select a search to edit.

Edit dialog for saved search

Set the name, query and icon v2.8.8, choose a filter chip if needed, and tap Save. Filters are saved with the search. To run a saved search, tap it in the navigation drawer.

Tip

Long-press a tag on the Tags screen to save it as a search. Saved searches can be included in backups.

items.title: Storage Manager
items.text:
The Storage Manager shows and manages files in the app's private storage.

To open it, go to Android Settings > Apps > Zettel Notes > Storage and Cache > Manage Space

It lists internal repositories, App Folder, Cache, Fonts and Database files, sorted by size.

items.title: Tasker Integration
items.text:
Tasker is a popular automation application for Android.

Zettel Notes supports integration with Tasker through its New Note Action Plugin. This allows you to create notes using dynamic variables for the title and content in a pre-selected location.

items.title: How to Create a Tasker Action
items.text:
1. Install Tasker.
  2. Open Tasker and create a new task.
  3. From the Plugin > Action category, select Zettel Notes.
  4. Configure the plugin by entering Tasker variables for the note’s content and filename.

items.title: Available Actions
items.text:
1. Create Note
  2. Get Note Content
  3. List Notes
Zettel Notes in Tasker plugins Create note tasker action settings Tasker action

items.title: Trigger Notes Scanner via Intent
items.text:
• Use the Send Intent action in Tasker.
  • Use the following details:
  • Action: org.eu.thedoc.zettelnotes.action.SCAN_NOTES
  • Extra: EXTRAS_REPOSITORY:<REPOSITORY_NAME>
  • Package: org.eu.thedoc.zettelnotes
  • Target: Service
  • Replace <REPOSITORY_NAME> with the name of the repository to scan.

items.title: Templates
items.text: Templates are reusable starting text for new notes.

items.title: Dynamic variables
items.text:
These variables can appear anywhere in a template and are replaced when the note is created:

  • $id$ : Note ID
  • $title$ : Note Title
  • $filename$ : Filename
  • $$yyyyMMdd$$ : Date variable
  • $uuid$ : A random UUID v2.9.9
  • $default-text$: Add Repository Default Text
  • $custom$ : Custom variable

$uuid$ also works in text snippets.

Tip

Date variables use two $ on each side. See SimpleDateFormat for the pattern syntax.

items.title: Custom Variables
items.text:
Any other name between single $ signs, e.g. $custom$, is a custom variable. When you create a note from the template, you are asked for its value, and every occurrence is replaced.

Usage of custom template variable

items.title: Default template
items.text: To make a template the default, long-press it and select Set as Default. It is then applied to every fleeting note created with the add button in the notes list.

items.title: Sharing Web Pages
items.text:
Share a web page from your browser to Zettel Notes to save it as Markdown. The following options appear in the share menu:

  1. New Note: create a note from the page content
  2. Add to Note: add the page URL to an existing note
  3. New Bookmark Note: create a note that opens the URL
  4. New Video Note: for YouTube videos
  5. Add Webpage Content to Note: download the page, convert it to Markdown and append it to a note you choose

Info

To change the default format for bookmark notes, video notes and web clips, go to Settings > Note Formats. Video note formats can use a $description$ variable for the video description v3.0.4.

For pages that require a login, use the built-in HTML-to-Markdown converter v2.6.1.

items.title: Sharing text and images
items.text:
• Text shared from any app can create a new note, be appended to an existing note, or be added to the Memo.
  • Images: when you share several images at once, they can be added to a single note v2.9.6.
  • When creating a note from a share, you can choose the subfolder; the last folder you chose is remembered v2.8.4.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
A note in Zettel Notes is a plain-text file with a supported extension (e.g. md, org, txt). Zettel Notes indexes every file in a repository for fast search.

Edits are saved directly to the file, so any other app can read your notes and you are never locked in.

Tip

For full list of supported file extensions, checkout Repository

items.title: Viewer and Editor Modes
items.text:
Every note has two modes:

  • View mode
  • Edit mode

View mode shows the rendered Markdown. Its layout depends on the note type.

Edit mode is where you write with Markdown formatting and insert tags, authors and links. See also Zettelkasten method.

items.title: Note Information
items.text:
In view mode, tap the top-right menu button to open Note Information.

Note Info Dialog

The dialog shows details such as word and character count, read time and backlinks. From it you can also:

  • rename the note v2.8.4
  • delete the note v2.7.4
  • share the note
  • see the note's UID by long-pressing its title v2.9.9

Info

Notes can be shared in several formats. See Share Notes.

items.title: Note Creation Date
items.text:
Android does not record when a file was created, and synced files lose that information anyway (see issue #392). To show a reliable creation date in the Notes List, store it in the filename or in the frontmatter.

If neither is present, the Notes List shows the file's Last Modified time.

Warning

After changing repository or template settings, tap Save in the lower-right corner or the change is lost.

items.title: Method 1: Date in the filename
items.text:
Go to Repositories > Edit Repository and set Date Format to yyyyMMddHHmmss.

New notes are then named like 20261028143000.md, and the Notes List shows that date and time.

items.title: Method 2: Date in the frontmatter
items.text: Add date: $$yyyyMMddHHmmss$$ to the frontmatter of new notes. When the note is created, the variable is replaced with the current date and time. You can do this in either of two places.

items.title: In repository default text
items.text:
Go to Repositories > Edit Repository and add this to Default Text (or add the date line to frontmatter that is already there):

---
date: $$yyyyMMddHHmmss$$
---

items.title: In a template
items.text:
Go to Templates > Edit Template and include the date line in the template's frontmatter:

---
title: "$title$"
date: $$yyyyMMddHHmmss$$
tags:
---

# $title$

Note

If the template also includes $default-text$ and the repository default text already sets date, remove one of them to avoid a duplicate key.

items.title: Display format
items.text: To change how dates are shown in the Notes List, Gallery and Recycle Bin, go to Settings > Theme > Misc > App-Wide Date Format.

items.title: Memo
items.text:
v3.1.0

The Memo is a scratchpad for quick capture: jot something down now and sort it into a proper note later.

Note

Memo was called Draft Notes before version 3.1.0.

items.title: Open the memo
items.text:
You can reach the memo from:

  • the Memo widget on your home screen (Widgets)
  • the right drawer, from any note (Navigation)
  • the Memo editor button in the editor toolbar

items.title: Add to the memo
items.text:
• Share text from any app to Zettel Notes and choose to add it to the memo v3.0.8.
  • Long-press the memo editor button to add text to the memo without leaving the note you are editing v3.0.8.

items.title: Pin, export and import
items.text:
• Long-press a memo entry to pin or unpin it v3.1.1.
  • Memo entries can be exported and imported, for example to move them to another device v2.9.9.

items.title: Note Types
items.text: Every note type is a plain-text file; the type is set by the note_type frontmatter property. Only view mode differs between types; edit mode is the same.

items.title: Task Note
items.text:
---
note_type: task
---

This note shows all the markdown style tasks as a simple task list. You can toggle task or add new task from the floating add button. To delete task swipe from left on the task and click on delete button. You can also show / hide completed tasks.

Task note options:

  • Swipe a task to rename or delete it; drag tasks to reorder them.
  • After checking a task, an Undo option appears v2.9.9.
  • In Settings > Note Formats you can strike through completed tasks, delete tasks when they are checked, or show each task on a single line v2.9.8.
  • A Task Note widget shows the tasks on your home screen.

Tip

It is possible to set alarm on a task. Just install Alarm Plugin and swipe on a task to set alarm.

Task Note

items.title: Drawing Note
items.text:
---
note_type: drawing
---

Collects your drawings in one place. Tap the floating + button to add a drawing.

Drawing Note

Tip

To change brush size, long press on the color selection button in lower right corner.

The suffix for newly created attachments (including recording, drawing, images) can be modified in settings. Go to Settings > Editor and Viewer > Attachment Suffix. It supports these variables ($$-yyyy-MM-dd$$ $id$ $title$ $filename$). Using $$-yyyy-MM-dd$$ variable will create drawing with file name as Drawing-2023-10-18.png. Id, Title and Filename will be populated from the note file.

Doodle Screen

items.title: Audio Note
items.text:
---
note_type: audio
---

Works as a voice recorder. Use one audio note to collect a series of voice memos, e.g. while travelling.

Audio Note

Info

To configure audio recording, go to Settings > Audio Recorder. You can configure Bitrate, Channel Count, Sampling Rate, Recording format and Filename.

items.title: Bookmark Note
items.text:
---
note_type: bookmark
url: https://thedoc.eu.org
---

Opens the URL in its frontmatter. With the example above, tapping the note in the notes list opens https://thedoc.eu.org in your browser.

To create a bookmark note, share webpage from browser and select Zettel Notes > New Bookmark Note from share screen.

items.title: Log Note
items.text:
---
note_type: log
---

Inspired by the .LOG feature of Windows Notepad: each time you open the editor, a timestamp is added on a new line. An option adds new entries at the beginning of the note instead of the end v2.9.6.

Info

To configure date format for log notes, go to Settings > Note Formats > Log Note > Date Format. Eg. To make log entry bold, use this date format '**'yyyy-MM-dd'**'

items.title: YAML Frontmatter
items.text:
Zettel Notes supports YAML frontmatter for note properties. The frontmatter must be the first thing in the note, enclosed by --- lines. For example, this sets the title to Note Title:

---
title: Note Title
---

This is body of the note.

The following properties are supported:

  1. title – The title of the note.
  2. tag(s) or keywords – One or more tags associated with the note. keywords is read for compatibility with Zettlr v3.0.2.
  3. author(s) – The author(s) of the note.
  4. source or url – The original source or URL reference.
  5. bookmark, pin, or star – Used to mark important notes.
  6. id or uid – Must match the repository's UID regex.
  7. date – At least 6 digits, typically in the format yyyyMMddHHmmss.

To specify multiple sources for a note, use array format. eg.

---
source:
      - https://google.com
      - https://gmail.com
---

Tip

YAML frontmatter can also be specified as default text for notes that will be added to new notes in repository settings

items.title: Org-mode notes
items.text:
In .org notes, the note ID can be set with an Org properties drawer v3.0.0:

:PROPERTIES:
:ID: fedcba98-7654-3210-fedc-ba9876543210
:END:

Org-roam style links are recognised too v2.9.9:

[[id:fedcba98-7654-3210-fedc-ba9876543210][Linked Note Title]]

items.title: YAML Variables
items.text:
Reference any frontmatter property in the note body with ${property}$.

---
account: savings
---

We should have at least ${account}$ type of account.

This will render as We should have at least savings type of account in view mode.

The following built-in variables are also available; their values come from the note itself.

  • ${id}$
  • ${title}$
  • ${filename}$
  • ${mdate}$ (Last modified date)
  • ${accessed}$ (Number of times note is opened)
  • ${wordcount}$
  • ${$yyyyMM$}$
  • In this variable yyyyMM will be replaced by the corresponding date time. To learn more about this format read official documentation.

Info

To disable YAML variables, toggle Settings > Editor and Viewer > YAML variables.

items.title: Editor
items.text:
To edit a note, tap the Edit button in view mode.

Tip

To open notes directly in edit mode, set Settings > Editor > Default Mode to Edit.

The editor has a text area in the centre and a row of editor buttons at the bottom of the screen.

Editor

By default, the editor places the cursor at the last edited position. To change this, go to Settings > Editor and Viewer > Initial Cursor Position and choose one of:

  1. Start of note
  2. End of note
  3. Last edit position
  4. None (Don't set initial cursor)

items.title: Editor Buttons
items.text: The editor buttons are shown in a row at the bottom of the screen. You can scroll right and left to see them all, press and hold to see the title of a button, and use the Settings button to change the order in which they're shown.

items.title: Markdown Buttons
items.text:
• This is the first editor button.
  • Eleven Markdown buttons are provided by default.
  • Clicking on the button will enter specific markdown format (e.g. ** for bold) in editor.
  • If you select some text and then click on markdown button, then that text will be surrounded with markdown format defined in the button.
  • To add new markdown button, just select edit button (floating pencil button).
  • Each Markdown button can have its own icon v2.8.3.
Markdown Buttons

items.title: Heading button
items.text:
• Click to insert heading format in front of line.
  • You can remove heading or add heading from Level 1 to Level 6 heading.

  2. Insert Authors
  3. Insert Note Link

items.title: Attachment button
items.text:
The folder where attachments are stored is defined by attachment location in repository.

  • Link
  • Audio recording
  • Drawing
  • Camera Image
  • File from storage
  • Media file from Gallery

Info

You can also download the link, if it is an image file.

items.title: Search and replace
items.text: The search and replace button finds text in the note and replaces it. Regular expressions are supported v2.9.3, and the replacement can be empty to delete matches.

items.title: Other buttons
items.text:
• Download online images: downloads online images in the note to local storage v2.4.4.
  • Meta keys toolbar: shows a row of keys such as Ctrl and arrows, for keyboard shortcuts on touch screens v2.9.1.
  • Clean sync tags: cleans up sync tags in the note v2.7.6.
  • Memo: opens the Memo; long-press to add text to it.
  • Add Icon: inserts an icon v2.8.3

items.title: Revision (Note History) Button
items.text:
Zettel Notes stores patch or diff of changes made in a note. You can browse and restore previous revisions of a note with this button.

Previous Revisions of a Note

items.title: Coffee Button
items.text: Keeps the screen awake for a set time (5, 10 or 30 minutes). Tap to start; long-press to stop.

items.title: Text Snippets Button
items.text:
A text snippet has 2 parts: Expander and Expansion. When a user taps on an expander, its expansion will be entered in the editor at the selected position.

For example, if the expander is otoh and the expansion is on the other hand, clicking on the expander otoh in Text Snippets will enter on the other hand in the editor. See the built-in "Heading with Subtasks" snippet for example.

The expander may also contain date and/or time placeholders in SimpleDateFormat; surrounding these with $$ will cause the expansion to expand them using the current date and time. For example, $$yyyy-MM-dd (EE)$$ will be expanded to the current date, formatted like 2024-07-26 (Fri).

To add a new text snippet or edit an existing one, just tap on the floating edit button.

Tip

You can quickly search for and insert text snippets by typing :? or :: while editing. Text snippets can also use the $uuid$ variable.

items.title: Citations Button
items.text:
This button is integrated with BibTex manager

Click to enter citation and long press button to generate bibliography.

items.title: Emoji Button
items.text:
Application has support for converting Emoji alias (in edit mode) to emojis (in view mode). Eg. :smile: is converted to 😄 in view mode. Clicking on an emoji will insert its alias in editor.

Info

For full list of supported emojis and aliases, follow this link

Emoji Button

items.title: Focus Mode Button
items.text:
Click to enable / disable focus mode while editing.

Focus Mode

Tip

You can enable Focus Mode for all notes from Settings > Editor and Viewer > Focus Mode.

items.title: Insert Table Button
items.text: Insert Table

items.title: Settings Button
items.text:
You can configure the order of editor buttons or enable / disable editor buttons with this button. Click on add button in setting screen to add groups. All the buttons below a group will be added in the group. Swipe a button to remove it from the toolbar.

Tip

Tap a group to change its icon and the number of columns it shows v2.8.4. The icon of every built-in button can be changed too.

The toolbar layout can be included in backups.

items.title: Typing shortcuts
items.text:
Type these while editing to open a picker:

Type To insert [[ a link to a note #? a tag @? an author :? or :: a text snippet

The trigger text can be changed, and given several aliases separated by spaces, in Settings > Editor and Viewer > Text Shortcuts v3.0.0. They can also be turned off.

items.title: Links in the editor
items.text: Long-press a link in the editor to open it v2.9.6. In view mode, long-press a link to see its URL.

items.title: Editor settings
items.text:
These options are in Settings > Editor and Viewer:

Setting Effect Auto-Save when Idle Saves the note automatically after a pause; the timeout can be changed Large headings Shows headings in proportionate sizes while editing Line numbers Shows line numbers in the editor Line wrap Wraps long lines in the editor and viewer Margins Changes the note margins Spellcheck Turns the keyboard spellchecker on or off Automatic list numbering Continues ordered lists automatically Highlight double-space endings Marks lines ending with two spaces (a Markdown line break) v3.0.8 Focus Mode Enables focus mode for all notes

A YAML checker in the editor flags invalid frontmatter v2.7.8.

items.title: Formatting
items.text: Zettel Notes follows the CommonMark Markdown specification, with the extensions listed below.

items.title: Bold
items.text:
• Enclose text with ** or __ eg. **text** or __text__
  • Rendered as text

items.title: Italics
items.text:
• Enclose text with * or _ eg. *text* or _text_
  • Rendered as text

items.title: Spoiler
items.text:
• Enclose text with >! and !<, e.g. >!hidden text!<
  • Click to reveal text in viewer mode
  • You can also long press to copy text in spoiler

items.title: Strike-through
items.text:
• Enclose text with ~~ eg. ~~strike~~
  • Rendered as ~~strike~~

items.title: Superscript
items.text:
• Enclose text with ^ eg. ^superscript^
  • Rendered as superscript

items.title: Subscript
items.text:
• Enclose text with ~ eg ~subscript~
  • Rendered as subscript

items.title: Text Highlight
items.text:
• Enclose text with == eg ==highlight==
  • Rendered as highlight

items.title: Heading
items.text:
• Heading is defined as # in front of text
  • 6 Heading levels are supported
  • eg. # Heading is interpreted as Heading level 1 and ## Heading as level 2

items.title: Code Highlighting
items.text:
• Two types of code formatting are supported:
  • Inline code code
  • Enclose text with single backtick (`)
  • Code blocks
  • Enclose text with three backticks (```) and a new line.
Code blocks

Code blocks are syntax-highlighted when you name the language after the opening backticks, e.g. ```bash. Tap a code block in view mode to copy its contents.

  • For a dark code theme, tick Dark Theme in the Markdown style.
  • Syntax highlighting can be turned off in Settings > Editor and Viewer.

items.title: Link
items.text:
• To create a link enclose the description in brackets and link in parentheses.
  • Eg. [Official Website](https://thedoc.eu.org)
  • Rendered as Official Website
  • You can also directly create link without description <https://thedoc.eu.org>.

items.title: Lists
items.text:
• Unordered (- Unordered)

  • Unordered (- Unordered)

  • Ordered (1. Ordered)

  • Ordered (2. Ordered)

items.title: Blockquote
items.text:
• Add > at the start of a line, e.g. > this is a blockquote

this is a blockquote

items.title: Task lists
items.text:
Defined via - [ ] in front of text. It is rendered only when bracket is the first thing in line.

Tasks can be ticked from View Mode

  • [ ] Pending with empty bracket
  • [x] Completed with x or X in bracket

items.title: Custom checkboxes
items.text:
The character in task bracket can be modified to show different statuses. The following custom checkboxes are supported:

  • - [-] Cancelled
  • - [!] Important
  • - [?] More Info
  • - [>] Scheduled.

items.title: Thematic break
items.text:
• Use ---, ***, ___ in a new line
  • rendered as

items.title: Comments
items.text:
• Following formats are supported
  • [comment]: This is a comment
  • %%comment%%
  • Comments are not shown in View Mode

items.title: Tables
items.text:
• Defined as
|Column 1 | Column 2 |
|---------|----------|
| Row 1   | Row 1    |
| Row 2   | Row 2    |
  • It will be rendered as
Column 1 Column 2 Row 1 Row 1 Row 2 Row 2

items.title: Images
items.text:
• Defined as ![Description](image-location.png)
  • Image location has to be relative to the note file or use / in start if absolute location is used.
  • Obsidian-style embeds such as ![[image.png]] are also supported. The format used when inserting images can be changed in Settings > Editor and Viewer.
  • ![](file.pdf) shows a preview of a PDF. See Gallery and Media for viewing, editing and pasting images.
  • To centre an image, wrap it in <center> tags.

Tip

To use specific width for images use HTML format. For eg. to set image width as 50%, use <img src="https://picsum.photos/id/237/1024/800" width="50%"/>

items.title: Footnotes
items.text:
Footnotes allow you to add references for specific text in a note.

To create a footnote, add [^1] after the text, e.g. Text[^1]. The identifier (1) can be any number or word without spaces. Then define the footnote at the end of the note, e.g. [^1]: This is the reference.

items.title: LaTeX
items.text:
Inline LaTeX

Enclose the formula in single $, e.g. $E = mc^2$.

Block LaTeX

Enclose the formula in $$ on separate lines:

$$
\int_0^1 x^2 \, dx = \frac{1}{3}
$$

Tip

The single-$ inline syntax can be turned off in settings if it conflicts with prices or other uses of $. LaTeX also renders in notes shared as PDF.

items.title: Maps
items.text: ![map](latlong:LATITUDE,LONGITUDE) shows a map image for that location. The Location plugin can insert the current location.

items.title: Colours
items.text: Hex colour values such as #FF5722 are displayed as colours in view mode v2.9.6.

items.title: Supported HTML tags
items.text:
• Blockquote (blockquote)
  • Center (center)
  • Code (code, pre)
  • Collapsible section (details, summary) v2.9.7
  • Emphasis (<i>, <em>, <cite>, <dfn>)
  • Heading (h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6)
  • Highlight (mark)
  • Keyboard input (kbd)
  • Link (a)
  • Lists (ul, ol)
  • Strong Emphasis (<b>, <strong>)
  • Superscript (<sup>)
  • Subscript (<sub>)
  • Strike-through (<s>, <strike>, <del>)
  • Spoiler (spoiler)
  • Underline (<u>, ins)

items.title: Tags
items.text: Tags are labels that facilitate efficient organization and retrieval of your notes.

items.title: Creating Tags
items.text:
Type hash (#) followed by keyword. Eg. #tag.

To add tags in YAML frontmatter, use tags: (tag: also works):

---
tags:
    - tag
    - tag with space
---

Note

For tags with space, special formatting (e.g., #tag with space#) is required when creating tag in content.

In YAML, tag values may contain commas.

items.title: Escaping
items.text: To write a # or @ that should not become a tag or author, put a backslash before it, e.g. \#not-a-tag v3.0.8.

items.title: Nested / Hierarchical Tags
items.text:
These tags are used to create convenient taxonomies.

Use forward slashes (/) to create hierarchies. Eg. #sports/football and #sports/cricket.

items.title: Tag Format Rules
items.text:
Letters, numbers, underscore (_), hyphen (-), and forward slash (/) are allowed.

Tags are case-insensitive and will display casing of first occurrence. For instance, if you create #Tag and later add #TAG, both will be displayed as #Tag.

items.title: Searching Tags
items.text: Use #tag in your search or click on a tag in a note.

items.title: Zettelkasten Method
items.text: Zettel Notes has first-class support for the Zettelkasten method.

items.title: Backlinks
items.text: Backlinks are notes that link to the current note. In note information dialog, all note backlinks are listed. You can click on any backlink note to open it.

items.title: Wiki style links
items.text:
Type [[ in the editor to pick a note and insert a link to it, e.g. [[note.md]].

Tip

To configure note links, go to Settings > Editor > Link Style. You can select among [[filename]], [[filename.md]], [[filename|title]], [[filename.md|title]], [[date]], [[date]] title, [title](filename), [title](filename.md) and [Title](../Filename.md).

Links can be relative to the current note, e.g. [[../file.md]] v2.7.2. To always insert absolute links (from the repository root), enable the absolute note links option in Settings > Editor and Viewer. Spaces in []() links are written as %20.

To create folder links, enter the absolute or relative folder path and add '/' at the end of link eg. [sub-folder](/sub-folder/). Clicking on this link will open the sub-folder folder.

Notes can also be linked using their id. The id is derived from the filename or the id property in the YAML frontmatter. You can configure the id detection pattern (regex) in the repository settings.

items.title: Tags
items.text:
• Tags are denoted by #tag or specifying tag in yaml
  • Type #? to show tag search dialog
  • Read More

items.title: Authors
items.text:
• Authors are denoted by @author or specifying author in yaml
  • Type @? to show author search dialog

items.title: New Note from selection
items.text:
You can create new note from selected text in editor. Just select some text in editor and click on Extract Note editor button in Editor

Extract note editor button

items.title: Table of contents
items.text:
To display table of contents, add [TOC] anywhere in the note.

To enable table of contents for all notes, tick Table of Contents (TOC) settings option in Settings > Editor and Viewer.

Tip

Table of contents can be customized per note using the following [TOC:min=1,max=2,symbol=round] syntax. Following symbols are supported arrow ➔,check ✔,circle ◯,dash -, diamond ◆,dot •, dot_large ⬤,square ■,star ★,and triangle ▶. Here min and max are the minimum and maximum heading levels to use.

items.title: Inline Heading links
items.text:
To create inline heading links add # in front of link eg. [Heading](#heading). Clicking on inline heading link will scroll to the specific heading. You will need to replace spaces and non-alphanumeric characters in heading with hyphen in the link.

Example

Inline link for # This is a heading will be [link](#this-is-a-heading).

items.title: Learn more about Zettelkasten method 📖
items.text:
The Zettelkasten method builds knowledge from short notes, each holding a single idea, that are densely linked to each other.

For a thorough introduction, see zettelkasten.de/introduction.

items.title: Share Notes
items.text:
A note can be shared as:

  • Launcher shortcut
  • PDF or HTML
  • Pinned Notification
  • via Pandoc as DOCX, EPUB, ODT, HTML
  • Zettel Links
  • an image v2.8.8
  • rendered HTML copied to the clipboard v2.9.6
  • the note file itself, sent directly to another app (e.g. email or Telegram)
  • a template

To copy or move notes to another folder, select them in the notes list.

Tip

You can also create note widgets. Read more.

items.title: Launcher Shortcuts
items.text:
A launcher shortcut opens a note directly from your home screen.

Tip

To create launcher shortcuts for media files, go to Gallery

Tap the menu button next to the note, choose Share > Create Launcher Shortcut, then place the shortcut on your home screen.

Note Share dialog

The following shortcut types are available:

  • Open Quick Note
  • New Drawing / Audio / Task / Note shortcut
  • Fleeting note shortcut
    • Directly open editor in selected repository
  • Fleeting note shortcut with template
    • Directly open editor with note populated from user selected template in selected repository
  • Folder shortcut
    • Opens app in user selected folder and repository.
  • Search shortcut
    • Open app with search bar focused.
  • Daily note shortcut v2.8.3
    • Opens today's daily note. If a daily note for today already exists, including one created on another device and synced, it is opened instead of a new one being created.
  • Most accessed notes
    • Shortcuts for the notes you open most often.
  • Sync shortcuts v2.4.4
    • Run synchronization in download-only or upload-only mode.

You can change a shortcut's label when you create it v2.6.8.

items.text: A quick settings tile creates a new drawing note from the notification shade. Add it by editing your quick settings tiles.

items.title: Pinned Notification
items.text:
Pin a note as a notification for quick access.

Tap the menu button next to the note and choose Share > Pin note as notification. To remove it, expand the notification and tap Close.

Pinned notification

items.title: Share via Pandoc
items.text:
To export a note with Pandoc, tap the menu button next to the note. Choose Share > via Pandoc > as DOCX / EPUB / HTML / ODT

Info

Termux needs to be installed for this.

One-time setup:

  1. Install Termux

    • Installing Termux application allows us to execute command line instructions (you will only have to setup it once, then Zettel Notes will use it as an intermediary for format conversions).
    • Download via Play Store or F-droid (Recommended).

  2. Grant Zettel Notes permission to access Termux by clicking on first button in dialog

  3. Select the output file format

  4. Configure storage access in Termux.

    • To do this you need to open Termux and type the command termux-setup-storage.
    • On Android 14, if Termux reports an aborted operation, run pkg install termux-am and then termux-setup-storage again.

  5. Enable external application access in Termux.

    • To enable it you have to edit from Termux itself its properties file ~/.termux/termux.properties. Read more on Github
    • Or you can paste the following command in termux echo "allow-external-apps=true" >> ~/.termux/termux.properties

  6. Install Pandoc

    • To do this paste pkg install pandoc in termux.

  7. Enter absolute path for repository

    • Tell Termux the absolute address in Android of the repository of our notes. Something similar to /storage/emulated/0/<repository>.

  8. Click on export button

items.text:
To share a Zettel link, tap the menu button next to the note. Choose Share > as Zettel Link.

You can change the format of Zettel Link in Settings > Notes List > Zettel Link Format

For a repository named root containing note.md with ID 123456, the supported link formats are:

  • znotes://root/?id=123456

  • https://thedoc.eu.org/app-links/zettel-notes/root/?id=123456

items.title: Plugins
items.text:
Plugins are small companion apps that add features to Zettel Notes. They are installed separately from the Play Store or the F-Droid repository. Most add a button to the editor toolbar.

The main app is, and will remain, free. Some plugins are paid; buying them funds ongoing development.

items.text:

Plugins use the plugin API version of the app. After a major app update, update your plugins too.

items.title: Repository
items.text:
A repository is the root folder for a collection of notes, similar to a vault in Obsidian.

To create one, open the main menu, select Repositories and tap the floating + button.

Tip

Long-press the + button to create a repository in the app's private storage.

items.title: Managing repositories
items.text:
• Switch quickly: repositories are listed in the left drawer, and long-pressing the home button lets you change repository.
  • Hide repositories you rarely use, and sort the repository list.
  • Open on start: the app can load a specific repository, or the last opened note, when it starts.

items.title: Properties of a Repository
items.text: A repository has the following properties.

items.title: 1. Title
items.text:
Must be unique. It can be changed later.

Each repository also has an icon, shown in the repository list and the left drawer. You can change it in the repository settings v3.0.0.

items.title: 2. Default text
items.text:
This text will be added to new note files. You can use any of these variables $title$, $id$, $filename$, $$yyyyMMdd$$.

Tip

When using templates, you will have to add $default-text$ variable at start of template to add repository default text in the note file.

items.title: 3. Date Format
items.text: It contains date format which will be replaced with the present date and time when creating new note.

items.title: 4. BibTex file
items.text: Click to select BibTex file for citations from internal storage. Read More

items.title: 5. File Extension
items.text: Supported extensions: md, org,txt,text, mkd, mdwn, mdown, mdtxt, mdtext,markdown.

items.title: 6. Prefer Title From
items.text:
• Default
    • Uses the first available of:
    • YAML Metadata > First Heading > File name
  • YAML Metadata
    • YAML Property title: Note Title is used to set title as Note Title.
  • First Heading
    • First Heading # Note Title is used to set title as Note Title.
  • Filename
    • Filename Note Title.md is used to set title as Note Title.
  • First line v2.9.5
    • The first line of the note is used as the title, whether or not it is a heading.

items.title: 7. Default location for attachments
items.text:
• Main Folder
    • The root folder will be used for storing attachments
  • Same folder as note
  • Specific subfolder
    • Specific subfolder set by user will be used for storing attachments.
    • It should start with /
  • Subfolder in same folder as note

items.title: Additional properties
items.text:
Zettel Notes allows you to configure certain additional properties for each repository. These can be set by clicking the Edit button in the top-right corner of the repository dialog.

The properties are saved in the Zettel Notes configuration folder, under the specific path for that repository.

items.title: 1. UID Regex (uid_regex)
items.text:
• Defines how the id of a note is determined.
  • Example: If set to ^\d{6,}, and a note filename is 20201210 Note File.md, the note ID will be 20201210.
  • This ID can be used for linking between notes.

items.title: 2. Mount (mount)
items.text:
• Specifies whether the repository should be accessible via the Android Documents app.
  • Mounting internal repositories
    • Repositories can be accessed via the android Documents application.
    • To disable mounting internal repositories, go to Settings > Security and disable Mount internal repositories.

Tip

To unmount specific repository, hide the repository in Repository settings.

items.title: 3. Exclude files and folders (excluded_paths)
items.text:
v3.0.7

Define files and folders that should be "ignored" in this repository.

Enter a comma-separated list of patterns, for example:

excluded_paths = /backupFolder/,/*.tmp,/note-?.md

Clarification:

  • By the term "ignoring files and folders", we mean a repository setting that:
    • hides files and folders in the "Notes List",
    • hides tags in the Navigation Drawer "Attributes",
    • turns links to hidden files into "Note Link not valid".
    • hides backlinks to hidden files in the "Backlinks" tab of the Right Drawer and the "Info" window.
  • To format the path correctly, use the absolute link rule within the repository: the path must start with / (/Folder/,/File.md).
  • Patterns are matched against file and folder paths using / as the separator.
  • Spaces are allowed in file and folder names (/Example Folder/,/Example File.md).

Supported patterns:

  • A pattern ending with / matches a folder and everything inside it. Example: temp/ excludes the temp folder and all its files and subfolders.
  • * matches any number of characters. Example: *.md matches all Markdown files.
  • ? matches exactly one character. Example: note-?.md matches note-1.md or note-a.md, but not note-10.md.

items.title: 4. Exclude tags (excluded_tags)
items.text:
v3.1.2

Define tags that should be "ignored" in this repository. Enter a comma-separated list of tags:

excluded_tags = archive,private

items.title: Note Encryption
items.text: Encryption is configured per repository. To enable it, go to Repositories > Long press on a repository > Encryption

items.title: 1. End-to-End Encryption
items.text:
• All newly created notes in this repository will be encrypted.
  • Your password is securely stored in the Android Keystore.
  • The salt and other decryption details are embedded within each encrypted note file.
  • You can share encrypted notes with others (e.g., via email); the recipient only needs the password to decrypt them.

items.title: 2. Password-Based Encryption
items.text:
• Notes are encrypted using a user-defined password.
  • If you uninstall Zettel Notes (which clears the SALT) or forget the password, the notes cannot be decrypted.
  • Decryption is possible between Android devices if the same salt is used.
  • To do this, copy the salt from Settings > Encryption Salt
  • If two devices have the same salt and the user knows the password, encrypted notes can be shared and decrypted across devices.
  • Only an asymmetric password hash (using Argon2) is stored locally. This hash is used to verify the password during decryption.
  • The user password is never stored in Zettel Notes.
  • If the password is reasonably strong, it is not possible to recover it from the stored hash.

items.title: 3. OpenPGP Encryption
items.text:
• Notes are encrypted using a PGP key provided by an external OpenPGP application.
  • This is enabled through integration with OpenKeychain: Easy PGP.

items.title: 4. PGP Key Encryption
items.text:
• An in-app PGP key is used for encryption.
  • You can generate the key via Settings > Keys Manager
  • Note encryption and decryption are seamless, similar to End-to-End Encryption.

items.title: Encryption and search
items.text:
Encrypted notes are decrypted only when you open them. By default, their content is still indexed so that search can find them. To keep encrypted content out of the search index, change the option in Settings > Security.

Note history of encrypted notes is encrypted as well.

items.title: Import Notes
items.text: To import notes from another app, go to Repositories > Long Press Repository > Import Notes.

items.title: 1. StyleNote
items.text:
Notes can be imported from a StyleNote HTML export.

Export your notes from StyleNote as HTML, then select that file in the importer.

items.title: Supported protocols
items.text:
• Git
  • Dropbox
  • WebDAV
  • SSH / SFTP

items.title: Features
items.text:
You can sync a subfolder instead of the whole remote folder, e.g. only root/notes within root.

You can generate private and public ssh keys within Zettel Notes. Git and SSH synchronization support keys generated via Keys Manager. See Keys Manager

To sync every time a note is saved, enable Settings > Synchronization > Trigger sync on saving note.

items.title: Background synchronization
items.text:
To enable background sync, turn on Settings > Synchronization > Enable background synchronization

Optional constraints:

  • Only sync while device is charging
  • Only sync while on WiFi
  • Only sync when battery level is above defined level

Available intervals:

  • 5 mins v3.0.2
  • 10 mins v3.0.2
  • 15 mins
  • 30 mins
  • 1 hour
  • 3 hours
  • 6 hours
  • 12 hours
  • 24 hours

If syncing is slow, you can restrict it to run only while the app is in the background.

Tip

Sync settings can be overridden per repository, e.g. Wi-Fi only for one and charging only for another. Go to Repositories > <Repository> Setting > Edit Synchronization > Configure synchronization.

items.title: Manual synchronization
items.text:
To sync only manually, disable these options in Settings > Synchronization

  • Enable background synchronization
  • Trigger synchronization on
    • Application start
    • Saving note
    • Swipe refresh

Then sync by tapping the sync button in the left navigation drawer.

items.title: Configure Conflict Resolution
items.text:
Configure conflict handling in Settings > Synchronization with the Conflict Resolution and Merge Strategy options. These apply to all sync methods.

  • Conflict Resolution
    • Auto
      • The default strategy
    • Prefer Local Changes
      • Changes in Zettel Notes overwrite changes on the server
    • Prefer Remote Changes
      • Changes on the server overwrite changes in Zettel Notes
  • Merge Strategy
    • These options are enabled only for Auto Conflict Resolution strategy
    • 3 options are provided
      • Default
        • Merge changes from Zettel Notes and the server
      • Prefer Old Changes
        • Older changes win, from either side
      • Prefer New Changes (Preferred Option)
        • Newer changes win, from either side

items.title: Dropbox Synchronization
items.text: To set up Dropbox sync, go to Repositories > Setup Sync > Dropbox, sign in, and choose the folder to sync.

items.title: Git Synchronization
items.text:
Git synchronization works only with repositories in the app's private storage, because of Android storage restrictions.

To set it up, select Setup Git when creating a repository.

Dialog to Add Repository

Configure the following:

  • Repository Url
    • Url of the remote repository.
    • Could be https://.. or in the format <username>@<server>:/path/to/repo for SSH.
  • Checkout Branch
    • The git branch which contains your note files (should exist on remote server).
    • If no checkout branch is set then the default remote origin branch is chosen.
  • Commit profile
    • Enter name and email of committer
  • Commit message
    • You can modify the commit message. It can contain date format variable (same as in templates).
  • Username
    • Used for login. For SSH, this should match the username specified in the Repository URL.
  • Password or Token
    • Enter password or your personal access token
  • Key authentication
    • Tick if using ssh url and private keys
    • You can select private key from Keys Manager or enter your own key in private key
    • If your private key uses password, then enter it also.
GIT Settings

Tip

For GitHub, use a personal access token instead of your password.

items.title: Git settings
items.text:
• .gitignore: edit the repository's .gitignore from the Git settings v2.5.7.
  • Certificates: Git sync trusts both system and user-installed CA certificates, so servers with self-signed certificates work once their CA is installed on the device v2.1.4.
  • List Commits: browse the commit history and all branches of the repository.

items.title: How sync handles conflicts
items.text:
When a note changes, the app syncs with the Git server as follows:

  1. Commit: Any local changes made to the notes are first committed.
  2. Rebase: The app attempts to rebase the local changes with the changes from the server. This method integrates changes without creating unnecessary merge commits.
  3. Merge (if rebase fails): If conflicts arise during the rebase, the app falls back to a merge operation to combine the changes.
  4. Push: All the changes are pushed to the git server.

By default, local changes win when a conflict cannot be merged (Git's "ours" strategy). To change this, see Configure Conflict Resolution.

items.title: Keys Manager
items.text:
Keys Manager generates SSH keys for Git and SFTP sync. Open it from Settings > Keys Manager.

Supported algorithms:

  1. DSA (Digital Signature Algorithm)
  2. RSA
  3. ECDSA
  4. ED25519
Keys Manager Dialog

To use an existing key instead of generating one, import it into Keys Manager v2.7.6.

Tip

items.title: SFTP (SSH) Synchronization
items.text:
To set up SFTP sync, go to Repositories > Setup Sync > SFTP (SSH) and enter:

  • Host / IP Address
  • Port
  • User
  • Password
  • Private Key
  • To use private ssh key, tick Public Key Authentication
  • You can either select your private key from Keys Manager or enter your own key.
  • If your private key has password, then enter it in Private key Password field.
  • Remote path
  • Set complete path of folder containing your notes
Password login Private key login

items.title: WebDAV Synchronization
items.text:
To set up WebDAV sync, go to Repositories > Setup Sync > WebDav and enter the WebDAV URL, username and password.

To sync a subfolder, include it in the URL.

Tip

If your server uses a self-signed certificate, tick Trust Private Certificate.

Info

Dotfiles and dot-folders (e.g. .attachments/) are not synced.
